issue_context.title: IPv6 Compliance RFC4191: Processing Router Advertisements with Router Preference (Host Only) [v6LC.2.2.22]
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

250

### Used distribution

Embedded Linux - Debian-based

### Linux kernel version used

5.15.71-rt51+gc36e774d0d9a

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

aarch64

### Component

systemd-networkd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

**Purpose**: Verify that the HUT uses a Default Router List with preference values for Type B Host.

When there are two routers on the network and Router1 sends an RA with `Reserved Route Preference`, meanwhile Router2 sends an RA with `Low Preference` route.  Later, Router2 changes from `Reserved` to `High` route preference. This change in preference route ought to result in the host sending to Router2 as the default route.  Instead, it continues to use Router1 as the default router.

From [RFC4191](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4191.txt):

Section 2.1:
```
   Preference values are encoded as a two-bit signed integer, as
   follows:

      01      High
      00      Medium (default)
      11      Low
      10      Reserved - MUST NOT be sent
```

Section 2.2:
```
Prf (Route Preference)
    If the Reserved (10) value is received, the receiver MUST treat
    the value as if it were (00).
```

Section 3.1:

```
   Type B hosts use a Default Router List augmented with preference
   values, but ignore all Route Information Options.  They use the
   Default Router Preference value in the Router Advertisement header.
   They ignore Route Information Options.
```


### Unexpected behaviour you saw

The router with `Reserved Preference` was used instead of the `High Preference` router.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Please find attached a zip file containing two PCAP files, `legacy` and `networkd`.  The `legacy` PCAP shows the correct behavior.  It was recorded when our host was configured using Debian's legacy `/etc/network/interfaces` file and `networkd` was disabled and stopped.  The `networkd` PCAP shows incorrect behavior. It was recorded after configuring `networkd` to manage the interface.

Under the `networkd` folder, the PCAP file `v6LC_2_2_22c-Net0-20230707043553-filtered.pcapng` shows the incorrect behaviour. 

Packet 1: Router1 sends an RA with a `Default Router Preference` equal `Reserved`.
Packet 2: Router2 sends an RA with a `Default Router Preference` equal to `Low`.
Packet 6: Router2 sends an RA with a `Default Router Preference` equal to `High`.
Packet 8: Ping reply is sent via Router1, when it should have been sent via Router2.

Compare that with the PCAP showing the correct behaviour in the `legacy` folder, `v6LC_2_2_22c-Net0-20230705084630.pcapng`.

Packet 1: Router1 sends an RA with a `Default Router Preference` equal `Reserved`.
Packet 2: Router2 sends an RA with a `Default Router Preference` equal to `Low`.
Packet 5: Router2 sends an RA with a `Default Router Preference` equal to `High`.
Packet 7: Ping reply is sent via Router2

[2_2_22c - Processing Router Advertisements with Router Preference.zip](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/12076148/2_2_22c.-.Processing.Router.Advertisements.with.Router.Preference.zip)

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

#### Changing Router Preference High to Low
I have second variation where the router preference for Router1 was changed from High to Low, meanwhile Router2 had a preference of Medium.  The host continues to choose Router1 as the default router, when it should be choosing Router2.  This suggests `networkd` is not updating the router preference.  See PCAP files in attached zip.

[2_2_22d - Processing Router Advertisements with Router Preference.zip](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/12076417/2_2_22d.-.Processing.Router.Advertisements.with.Router.Preference.zip)

#### Changing Router Low to High
A third variation has Router1 changing from Low to High, meanwhile Router 2 had a preference of Medium.  The host continues to choose Router2 when it should be choosing Router1.

[2_2_22e - Processing Router Advertisements with Router Preference.zip](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/12076622/2_2_22e.-.Processing.Router.Advertisements.with.Router.Preference.zip)
comments: @LiveFreeAndRoam Thank you for finding many RFC incompliant behaviors in networkd. But, v250 is slightly old here. Could you test the behaviors in a recent release or the current git HEAD?

It's difficult for me to update, due to this being an embedded system. Though, I have scanned the release notes and there has been nothing mentioned about IPv6 improvements since v250.  If the release notes are accurate, then we can assume the behaviour will be the same.

Meanwhile, I do have a plan to try to upgrade to the latest and greatest. Ultimately, we need these fixes and I understand you will only be supporting the two most recent releases.  So I am motivated to get to the latest, but it's not a simple task at the moment.

OK. No problem. I have not read your reports in detail yet, but some of them are clearly not supported yet or wrongly implemented in networkd even on recent release. I will take a look. Feel free to open any other incompliance if you find (even that's on v250). Thank you again!

@LiveFreeAndRoam just out of curiosity I wonder if those issues have been found automatically using some sort of test suite where `networkd` is compared to `legacy` (which is known to be compliant)? I think if it's already automated somewhere (and can be shared) it would be great to somehow integrate it into the systemd CI to let it do its thing automatically and catch regressions. That part of networkd is being covered in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/28424 but it's more of a smoke test.

I'm using an IPv6 compliance test suite to identify non-conformance.  The test suite we use is a commercial product.  Though, in years gone by, I have used TAHI.  I can't vouch for whether it's still being maintained, but on their home page, they have links to their conformance test tools: https://www.ipv6ready.org/resources.html.

@yuwata, I merged your changes into my branch and reran the IPv6 Conformance tests, 2.2.22[abcde].  The signature has changed a little.  The results show:

* **2.2.22a** - PASS: Processed RA with high preference, no Echo Reply to TR1
* **2.2.22b** - FAIL: Didn't process RA with low preference, no Echo Reply to TR2
* **2.2.22c** - PASS: Processed RA with Reserved preference, Echo Reply to TR2
* **2.2.22d** - FAIL: No Echo Reply to TR2 after RA with a high preference
* **2.2.22e** - FAIL: No Echo Reply to TR2 after RA with Medium preference

Do those failure signatures provide enough information for you to tweak the solution to cover those cases?  If not, then I can go into much greater detail.  Let me know, either way.
Please also provide the debugging logs of networkd during the test with #31173.
I may find a root cause why #31173 does not work. I will try to update.
Let me know when you have it updated and I will retest.
